name: laws-of-ux
description: Audits a frontend project against the 30 Laws of UX (lawsofux.com). Detects the UI stack, scores each applicable law from concrete source-code signals, and produces a graded report (0-100 + A-F) with a findings table, a coverage band, and a prioritized quick-wins-vs-larger-efforts fix list. Static by default; an optional --url pass measures the running app. Read-only unless you run /ux-fix.

interface.shortDescription: Grade a frontend project against the 30 Laws of UX with code-level fixes
interface.longDescription: Walks a frontend codebase, detects the UI stack, and grades it against the 30 Laws of UX (Heuristics, Gestalt, Cognitive Biases, and general Principles) using concrete source-code signals. Applicability and detection-confidence are first-class: only laws it can actually assess move the grade, and every report states what it could not see. Produces a Markdown report plus an optional HTML scorecard in the shadcn/Geist visual style, a findings table with file:line evidence, and a prioritized quick-wins-vs-larger-efforts fix list. Static by default; an optional live pass measures the running app (performance, real tap-target geometry, rendered visuals). Read-only unless you opt into apply mode.
defaultPrompt: Audit my project against the Laws of UX
Grade the UX of this app and show me the fixes
Find usability issues in this frontend and prioritize them
